deep.reconstruction:
Context: the double sheet works with Riemann's normal form of the plane quartic (genus 3). Equation (9), on an earlier page, is presumably sqrt(x*xi)+sqrt(y*eta)+sqrt(z*zeta)=0, where x, y, z, xi, eta, zeta are linear forms, i.e. six bitangents ('Abelian functions' sqrt(x) etc.). The aim is to find, for the group of sqrt(x xi), sqrt(y eta), the remaining pairs of bitangents p, q whose product is a square on the curve.

(1) Form (15). A linear relation among the six forms, after rescaling (replacing lambda a, mu a by b, c), is a x + b y + c z + xi/a + eta/b + zeta/c = 0. Overall constant factors on p and q do not matter. One then sets
 p = a x + b y + c z = -(xi/a + eta/b + zeta/c),
 q = xi/a + eta/b + c z = -(a x + b y + zeta/c).
The second equality for q follows by substituting xi/a + eta/b = -(a x + b y + c z) - zeta/c.
[My filling-in of why this works:] Put P = a x + b y and Q = xi/a + eta/b. Then
 p q = P Q + c z (P + Q) + c^2 z^2 = P Q - z zeta = x xi + y eta - z zeta + (a/b) x eta + (b/a) y xi.
On the curve, z zeta = x xi + y eta + 2 sqrt(x xi y eta). Hence
 p q = (sqrt((a/b) x eta) - sqrt((b/a) y xi))^2,
so sqrt(p q) is rational in sqrt(x eta) and sqrt(y xi), and p, q are bitangents of the relevant group. Riemann says there are four such pairs, so there must be four systems (a, b, c).

(2) Counting. Among the six forms there are three independent homogeneous linear relations u1 = u2 = u3 = 0. A general combination is
 l1 u1 + l2 u2 + l3 u3 = alpha x + beta y + gamma z + alpha' xi + beta' eta + gamma' zeta,
with coefficients linear in the l_i. It takes the shape (15) exactly when alpha alpha' = beta beta' = gamma gamma' = k; dividing by sqrt(k) then gives a = alpha/sqrt(k) and alpha'/sqrt(k) = 1/a. These are two quadratic conditions on (l1 : l2 : l3) in P^2, so by Bezout there are four solutions.

(3) Normalization (16). Take three of these four relations as the defining relations:
 x+y+z+xi+eta+zeta = 0,
 alpha x + beta y + gamma z + xi/alpha + eta/beta + zeta/gamma = 0,
 alpha' x + ... + zeta/gamma' = 0.
The unit coefficients in the first relation are obtained by rescaling the six forms. Such a rescaling (presumably by reciprocal constants on each pair x, xi etc.) leaves the form of (9) unchanged.

(4) The fourth relation (17). It has coefficients alpha'', beta'', gamma'' and 1/alpha'', ... Since the relation space is 3-dimensional, (17) must be a combination:
 lambda''*(17) = (16a) + lambda*(16b) + lambda'*(16c).
Comparing the coefficients of x and xi (and likewise y, eta; z, zeta) gives (18):
 lambda'' alpha'' = lambda' alpha' + lambda alpha + 1,
 lambda''/alpha'' = lambda'/alpha' + lambda/alpha + 1,
and the same with beta, gamma.

(5) Equation (19). Multiplying each pair eliminates alpha'':
 lambda''^2 = lambda'^2 + lambda^2 + lambda lambda' (alpha/alpha' + alpha'/alpha) + lambda (alpha + 1/alpha) + lambda' (alpha' + 1/alpha') + 1,
and analogously for beta and gamma.

(6) Continuation on the following sheet. Subtracting the equations of (19) cancels lambda''^2, lambda^2 and lambda'^2. Dividing by lambda lambda' leaves two equations linear in 1/lambda and 1/lambda'. These fix lambda and lambda' uniquely; then lambda'' follows up to sign, and alpha'', beta'', gamma'' follow up to a common sign.
[My remark:] The linearity is explained by the counting. The two conics in (l1 : l2 : l3) meet in four points. Three of them are known: the given relations, corresponding to lambda = lambda' = 0, lambda = 0 and lambda' = 0. So the fourth is determined rationally.

The resulting four forms x+y+z, alpha x+..., alpha' x+..., alpha'' x+... are bitangents. This yields the 16 further bitangents listed on the following sheet.
errors: No mathematical errors found. (15), the two expressions for q, (18) and (19) all check out.
Implicit: dividing by sqrt(alpha alpha') to reach form (15) needs alpha alpha' not 0, and the sign choice of the root is left unstated (Riemann later notes the overall sign stays undetermined).

Implicit: the elimination leading to linear equations in 1/lambda, 1/lambda' (next sheet) silently discards the solutions with lambda = 0 or lambda' = 0. These correspond to the already-known relations, so this is legitimate but not said.
The claim that a rescaling of the six forms leaves (9) unchanged in form needs the scalings to be paired reciprocally (x with xi etc.), or the constants absorbed. This is not spelled out.

results.what: Normal form sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0 of a plane quartic and determination of further bitangent pairs p,q via linear relations of shape a x+b y+c z+xi/a+eta/b+zeta/c=0
results.modern_name: Riemann's normal form of the plane quartic; bitangents and theta characteristics (Steiner complexes / syzygetic groups)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, 'Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen fuer den Fall p=3' (Werke 1876, ed. Weber); Weber 1876; Aronhold 1864; Hesse, Steiner

results.what: Counting four relation systems as the intersection of two conics alpha alpha'=beta beta'=gamma gamma' in the (l1:l2:l3)-plane
results.modern_name: Bezout count; four pairs of bitangents in a Steiner group beyond the given ones

results.what: Rational determination of the fourth relation (alpha'', beta'', gamma'') from three given ones via equations (18)-(19), giving linear equations in 1/lambda, 1/lambda'
results.modern_name: Construction of the 28 bitangents from an Aronhold-type normal form; residual intersection point of two conics

deep.surprise_reason: This is the computation that appears in Riemann's posthumously published p=3 paper (Werke, ed. Weber), which is based on exactly such notes. It is already credited to Riemann and is a routine algebraic elimination.
